title: Current Use of Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling in New Medicinal Product Approvals at EMA

content.abstract_summary: EMA review of PBPK models in full-basis marketing-authorisation applications approved in 2022-2023, focusing on intended use, regulatory impact, qualification, and reasons models were not considered qualified. It shows that intended-use qualification, not structural plausibility alone, determines whether PBPK evidence can support decisions.
key_findings: Twenty-five of 95 full-basis applications contained PBPK modeling.
Across 65 proposed intended uses, enzyme/transporter DDI prediction was the most common at 69%.
Only 28% of applications containing PBPK models were considered qualified according to the EMA reporting guideline.
Qualification requires verification, validation against observed data, and evaluation against the question of interest.
Model impact and context determine the needed evidence and acceptance criteria.
limitations: The analysis covers EMA approvals from only 2022 and 2023.
Confidential submission details limit public transparency.
The review evaluates submitted PBPK evidence, not LLM-generated models.

extracted_claims.text: A PBPK model used as key regulatory evidence must be qualified for its intended use.
Qualification combines platform/equation verification, validation against observed data, and evaluation for the question of interest.
Most submitted models were not considered qualified for their intended uses.

numerical_findings.description: Intended uses involving enzyme/transporter DDI prediction
Applications with PBPK models considered qualified

gaps_addressed: Supports M4.5-A9 as a context-of-use qualification task and provides empirical regulatory anchors for DDI use and qualification scoring.

provenance.notes: Bibliographic metadata verified through PubMed. Open PMC full text reviewed at targeted sections covering study highlights, qualification definitions, results, and regulatory implications.
